claims.text: A 66-year-old man with no past medical history had fever, dry cough and vomiting one week before the onset of GBS symptoms, and was admitted to neurology in September 2020 with bilateral peripheral facial palsy, acute proximally pronounced symmetrical tetraparesis and acute headache. Examination showed graded limb weakness, areflexia, and numbness and tingling of all four limbs.
